findings.title: Concern, quantity, and assent
findings.claim: The focus places intense desire beside a majority still outside believer-status. Read with 10:99, where all people on earth could believe and the addressee is asked whether to compel them, the relation distinguishes wanting universal belief from having power to produce it.
findings.mechanism: The carriers are the focus's numerical majority head, intense-desire verb, and final believer-status predicate. The supplied 10:99 connection sets an all-people possibility beside an explicit question of compulsion; these contacts return through the focus's count, desire, and assent words and make their separation perceptible.
findings.reader_payoff: A strong wish for people to believe can be felt as sincere concern while the size of the group remains a count, not a lever over another person's assent.
findings.containment: The focus still states that most people are not believers. This does not diagnose why, equate the two audiences, or turn the target morphology of 10:99 into an independently verified analysis.

epistemic.reason: The focus branches and exact 10:99 Arabic are supplied, but both reader-walk supports are legacy_unbound and the target morphology is not supplied; the connection remains a bounded resonance.

findings.title: Belief as claim and status
findings.claim: Two wider echoes let the focus's final believer-status predicate carry both accepting testimony and being counted among believers: in 12:17 the brothers anticipate that their father will not believe their account even if truthful, while 2:8 separates people saying 'we believe' from the statement that they are believers. The focus can resonate with credibility and profession without assigning either scene to its majority.
findings.mechanism: The carrier is مُؤْمِنِينَ in the focus's negative predicate. The exact 12:17 target frames belief in a spoken account; the exact 2:8 target places a profession of belief beside denied believer-status. Their contact with the focus's predicate makes the distinction between a claim, its acceptance, and a status newly visible.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus's category of believers need not feel like a bare label: elsewhere the same belief field concerns whether a testimony is credited and whether a profession amounts to accepted status.
findings.containment: The brothers' line in 12:17 is their own claim, not proof that they are truthful; 2:8 does not license a judgment about the focus's audience or anyone's motive. Target morphology and lexical analysis are not supplied for either connection.

epistemic.reason: The HFT nomination is legacy_unbound and its 12:106 extension is excluded; the narrower claim is independently grounded by exact target Arabic in 12:17 and 2:8, whose target morphology remains unavailable.

findings.title: Signs and active turning-away
findings.claim: The focus names nonbelief without giving its cause. Beside 6:4, it can coexist with a wider picture in which signs arrive and people actively turn away, adding active non-reception as a possible reading without attributing that act to the focus's majority.
findings.mechanism: The carrier is the focus's final predicate مُؤْمِنِينَ under negation. The independent trigger is the exact 6:4 target surface and its supplied connection note: signs come, and the people turn away from them. Their contact places the focus's result beside an active posture of non-reception, changing the reader's view of what can accompany limited belief while leaving the focus's cause open.
findings.reader_payoff: Non-reception can be seen alongside both an unachieved wish and an active response to signs, without forcing those descriptions into one explanation.
findings.containment: 12:103 does not say that its people saw these signs or turned away. The 6:4 target morphology and lexical analysis are not supplied, and this connection is a wider parallel rather than a diagnosis of the focus.

epistemic.reason: The HFT summary is unanchored and its 12:105 detail is excluded; the retained narrower parallel rests on the exact 6:4 Arabic surface and the supplied focus-directed connection, without external morphology.

findings.title: Concern beside clear delivery
findings.claim: The focus's intense concern can sit beside a wider account of the messenger's role: when people turn away in 16:82, the supplied text leaves the addressee with clear delivery. The juxtaposition distinguishes earnest concern from control of the outcome.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier حَرَصْتَ expresses unusually strong desire; the independent 16:82 trigger says that if people turn away, clear delivery remains upon the addressee. Contact between intense concern and this bounded communicative role makes the focus's failed persuasion legible without making the desire itself an act of coercion.
findings.reader_payoff: The addressee can want a response deeply while the available act remains clear communication when listeners turn away.
findings.containment: The 16:82 audience and situation are not identified with Yusuf's audience, and this relation does not explain why most people do not believe. The target morphology is not supplied; the retrospective details from 12:104-111 are excluded.

findings.title: A repeated majority formula
findings.claim: Beyond the declared pericope, 12:21, 12:40, and 12:68 each place a majority beside not-knowing; 12:103 instead predicates nonbelief of most people. The recurrence lets epistemic and belief-status readings sit alongside one another in the surah without equating them.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier أَكْثَرُ is the measured majority head. The exact target Arabic and connection notes at 12:21, 12:40, and 12:68 repeat the majority-and-not-knowing formulation; at 12:40 it follows an explicit statement of the upright religion. This independent recurrence returns through the focus's numerical majority word and turns an isolated count into a wider pattern of majority response.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus's statement about believer-status can be heard next to repeated statements about what most people do not know, while each remains a distinct description.
findings.containment: The packet supplies target Arabic but not target morphology or lexical analyses. The recurrence does not mean ignorance causes nonbelief, that the predicates are equivalent, or that every majority response is the same.

epistemic.reason: Exact target surfaces and focus-word mapping are supplied, but the connection rows are nominations rather than verdicts and the target morphology is unavailable.
